title: Run and grow a town LoRa mesh
summary: How much text a town LoRa mesh can carry on each preset, what the firmware does as the air fills, and how messages find their way. Watch the network from one fixed node, find failing relays, and add neighbourhoods without clogging the air.

materials.item: Handheld Meshtastic node on the town's settings, for surveys, traceroutes and range tests
Fixed node that never moves, at the hub or NOMAD box, to watch the mesh
Laptop or small computer with the Meshtastic command-line tool, and a USB data cable (charge-only cables carry no data)

steps.text: Map the links: traceroute from the hub to each relay, at least 30 s apart. Draw each link on the map with its SNR both ways and the date. Mark links with under 5 dB margin above the preset's decode limit as weak (list in the notes).

Watch from the fixed node. Each week list the nodes (meshtastic --nodes) and log each relay's last-heard time and battery. For volts add --show-fields user.shortName,lastHeard,deviceMetrics.voltage. Ask a relay for fresh readings with meshtastic --request-telemetry --dest and its node ID.

Watch the air. If channel use (ChUtil) stays over 25 %, cut background traffic first: fixed positions and less position sharing, then telemetry. Leave NodeInfo alone. Before a faster preset, check every link's margin against its decode limit.
When a relay has not been heard for 6 hours, traceroute to it. Not heard for 24 hours, or traceroutes go around it: visit it with the spares kit (see the handover guide).
steps.warn: Never climb a mast or roof alone, when thunder can be heard, or until 30 minutes after the last thunder (NOAA lightning). Follow the climbing, power-line and lightning warnings in the town mesh guide.

steps.text: To add a neighbourhood, survey it with a handheld, check the saved Site Planner maps and range test from the nearest relay. Try a CLIENT_BASE on the best roof, with that area's nodes as favourites, before adding another ROUTER.

notes:
Build the mesh first: [Build a LoRa mesh node from parts](#guides/build_lora_node), [LoRa mesh network for a whole town](#guides/build_lora_town_mesh). Band rules: [LoRa bands](#ref/reference_lora_bands). Your own numbers: [LoRa airtime calculator](#ref/lora_airtime). Figures are for Meshtastic as of firmware 2.7 (source read at release 2.7.26); defaults change between releases. Handing the network over to the next keeper: [Hand over a town LoRa mesh](#guides/skill_lora_mesh_handover).

## Airtime per preset

A Meshtastic packet is one LoRa frame: a 16-symbol preamble, a radio header, the payload and a 16-bit CRC. The payload is a 16-byte Meshtastic header plus the encrypted message, 255 bytes at most (Meshtastic mesh algorithm, Meshtastic RadioInterface.h, RadioLib SX126x).

Time on air, calculated for this guide with Semtech's formula (SX1262 datasheet, section 6.1.4):

- Symbol time Ts (ms) = 2^SF ÷ BW (kHz).
- Symbols = 16 + 4.25 + 8 + ceil((8 × PL + 16 − 4 × SF + 8 + 20) ÷ (4 × SF)) × (CR + 4).
- PL is the packet in bytes, 16 the CRC bits, 20 the explicit header, CR 1 for 4/5 and 4 for 4/8. With low-data-rate optimisation the divisor is 4 × (SF − 2); the radio library turns it on for symbols of 16 ms or more, here Long Moderate and Long Slow (SX1262 datasheet, RadioLib SX126x).
- Packet sizes: a 10-letter text is 32 bytes, a 200-letter text 223 bytes: the 16-byte header, the text and 6–7 bytes of framing as firmware 2.7.26 encodes it (calculated for this guide from Meshtastic Router.cpp). 255 bytes is the largest packet. A direct message between nodes with keys is 12 bytes longer (public-key encryption): 44 bytes for 10 letters, 559 ms on Long Fast (calculated for this guide from Meshtastic Router.cpp, Meshtastic RadioInterface.h).

| Preset (Meshtastic presets) | SF, kHz, CR | 10 letters | 200 letters | 255 bytes | Short texts a minute to 25 % ChUtil: sent once / with 4 routers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Short Turbo | 7, 500, 4/5 | 20 ms | 90 ms | 102 ms | 748 / 149 |
| Short Fast | 7, 250, 4/5 | 40 ms | 181 ms | 204 ms | 374 / 74 |
| Short Slow | 8, 250, 4/5 | 75 ms | 321 ms | 362 ms | 199 / 39 |
| Medium Fast | 9, 250, 4/5 | 140 ms | 570 ms | 642 ms | 107 / 21 |
| Medium Slow | 10, 250, 4/5 | 259 ms | 1.04 s | 1.18 s | 57 / 11 |
| Long Turbo | 11, 500, 4/8 | 312 ms | 1.46 s | 1.66 s | 48 / 9 |
| Long Fast (default) | 11, 250, 4/5 | 477 ms | 1.91 s | 2.16 s | 31 / 6 |
| Long Moderate | 11, 125, 4/8 | 1.51 s | 7.02 s | 7.93 s | 9 / 1 |
| Long Slow (2.7 and older) | 12, 125, 4/8 | 2.76 s | 12.72 s | 14.30 s | 5 / 1 |

The 500 kHz Turbo presets are not legal in every region (Meshtastic presets).

**Text length.** The apps stop a message at 200 bytes, about 200 plain letters; the mesh payload limit is 233 bytes (Meshtastic Android messages). With the 16-byte header and 6–7 bytes of framing, 255 bytes is the cap, so the longest channel text is 232 bytes and the longest direct-message text 220 (Meshtastic Router.cpp). A 200-letter message costs four times the air of a 10-letter one: keep messages short.

## How fast the channel fills

Channel use = transmissions a minute × airtime ÷ 60 s. Each copy of a packet costs its full airtime again:

- **Every hop is one more transmission.** A message that crosses 3 hops is on the air at least 4 times.
- **Every router adds one.** ROUTER and ROUTER_LATE nodes rebroadcast each packet once even when they hear another node do it (Meshtastic mesh algorithm). Four routers that hear a message make at least five transmissions of it.
- **Retries.** A sender that hears no rebroadcast or acknowledgement sends again; a reliable broadcast goes out at most three times (Meshtastic mesh algorithm).

Worked example, calculated for this guide: 10 short texts a minute on Long Fast through 4 routers is 10 × 5 × 0.477 s ≈ 24 s a minute, 40 % channel use before any NodeInfo, position or telemetry. On Medium Fast: about 12 %.

Routers that are direct neighbours transmit together and collide, and raising the hop limit only adds airtime (Meshtastic role blog): few routers, hop limit 3.

**Europe, as an aside.** In EU_868 a node stops transmitting once it has sent for 10 % of the last hour, and its telemetry and NodeInfo stop at 5 % (Meshtastic LoRa, Meshtastic airtime.h, Meshtastic airtime.cpp, Meshtastic Router.cpp). The US region has no duty-cycle limit in the firmware (Meshtastic LoRa). Country rules: [LoRa bands](#ref/reference_lora_bands).

## When the air gets busy

- **ChUtil:** the share of the last minute this node spent sending or hearing LoRa, including packets it hears but cannot decode (damaged, or from other networks on the same settings) (Meshtastic airtime.cpp, Meshtastic airtime.h, Meshtastic RadioLibInterface.cpp).
- **AirUtilTX:** the share of the last hour this node spent sending (Meshtastic airtime.cpp).

Both are in device metrics, sent to a connected app every minute (Meshtastic telemetry). The firmware holds back its own broadcasts as ChUtil rises:

| Broadcast | Skipped above |
|---|---|
| Position | 25 % (TRACKER, TAK_TRACKER: 40 %) (Meshtastic PositionModule.cpp) |
| Device telemetry: clients / ROUTER, ROUTER_LATE, SENSOR | 25 % / 40 % (Meshtastic DeviceTelemetry.cpp) |
| NodeInfo sent to greet a newly heard node (never from ROUTER, ROUTER_LATE, CLIENT_BASE) | 25 % (Meshtastic MeshService.cpp) |
| NodeInfo reply to a request | 40 % (Meshtastic NodeInfoModule.cpp) |
| Environment telemetry (sensors) | 25 % (SENSOR role 40 %) (Meshtastic EnvironmentTelemetry.cpp) |

Typed messages and relayed packets are not held back by channel use. They wait for a clear channel and a random delay: your own messages wait longer as channel use rises, relays wait by signal strength (Meshtastic mesh algorithm, Meshtastic RadioInterface.cpp). Power telemetry from an INA219 or INA260 is not held back by channel use either, only by the EU duty-cycle limit (Meshtastic PowerTelemetry.cpp). The ROUTER_LATE blog tells anyone running ROUTER_LATE as a rooftop node to stop if ChUtil passes 25 % or the node's AirUtilTX passes about 7–8 % (Meshtastic ROUTER_LATE blog). That is advice for that role, not a limit for the whole mesh.

**Default intervals, firmware 2.7.26** (Meshtastic Default.h, Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp, Meshtastic mesh algorithm):

| Broadcast | Clients | ROUTER, ROUTER_LATE |
|---|---|---|
| NodeInfo | 3 h (1 h minimum) | 3 h |
| Position, only on channels with position precision above 0 | 1 h (15 min up to 2.7.17; an older node keeps its saved 15 min off the default channel) | 12 h |
| Device telemetry | off; set an interval when you turn it on (0 means 1 h) | off; 12 h when turned on (ROUTER_LATE 24 h) |
| Power and environment telemetry (off until turned on; needs a sensor) | 1 h | 12 h |

A clean node stores a device telemetry interval of "never". Turn telemetry on without setting an interval and it sends once, then waits about 25 days. Set the interval too and check it with `meshtastic --get telemetry` (a setting that is off or 0 is not listed). Changing a node's role to ROUTER sets 12 h, to ROUTER_LATE 24 h. On a mesh that keeps a default public channel (the preset's default name with the default key), the firmware raises shorter settings: telemetry to 30 minutes for clients and 12 hours for routers, positions to 1 hour for clients and 12 hours for routers (routers since 2.7.21) (Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp, Meshtastic Default.h). Smart position sends early only after the node has moved 100 m (Meshtastic position), and on 2.7.26 no sooner than 5 minutes after the last (Meshtastic Default.h).

**Above 40 nodes** heard in the last 2 hours, clients stretch position and telemetry intervals: on Long Fast by 8.2 % per extra node, so at 62 nodes an hour becomes about 2.8 hours. Routers, sensors and trackers don't stretch (Meshtastic mesh algorithm, Meshtastic Default.h).

**What to lengthen first:**

1. **Positions.** Give relays and home bases a fixed position, set position precision 0 on channels that don't need it, and lengthen handheld intervals.
2. **Telemetry.** Leave device telemetry off on handhelds (the default). On relays keep the long interval and ask for readings when you need them.
3. **NodeInfo last.** Leave it at 3 h: a direct message needs the other node's public key, which comes in NodeInfo, and 2.7.26 refuses to send one without it (Meshtastic Router.cpp).

Wellington's channel use peaked over 65 % on Long Fast, largely NodeInfo, position and telemetry updates from clients (Meshtastic LongFast blog).

**Node counts.** Meshtastic suggests leaving Long Fast past about 60 nodes close together (Meshtastic LongFast blog). A node's list holds 80 nodes on nRF52 boards, 100 on ESP32, 200–250 on an ESP32-S3 with 8–16 MB flash; when full, the oldest non-favourite is dropped (Meshtastic node limits, Meshtastic NodeDB.cpp). Mark every relay and admin handheld as a favourite on each relay.

## How packets cross the mesh

This adds to the town guide's [Roles: few routers](#guides/build_lora_town_mesh).

- **Far nodes go first.** A node waits before repeating a new broadcast; weak (far) signals get a short wait, so the node covering most new ground repeats first (Meshtastic mesh algorithm). The firmware maps SNR from −20 dB (shortest) to +10 dB (longest) and gives a ROUTER a window that ends before any other role's begins (Meshtastic RadioInterface.cpp). On Long Fast a slot is about 28 ms, so routers repeat within about 0.4 s and others wait 0.45 s to about 7.6 s (calculated for this guide: slot = 2.5 symbols + 7.6 ms, Meshtastic RadioInterface.cpp).
- **Cancelling.** A CLIENT that hears another node repeat the packet first drops its own copy. ROUTER and ROUTER_LATE never do; CLIENT_BASE never does for packets to or from its favourites; CLIENT_MUTE never repeats (Meshtastic FloodingRouter.cpp).
- **Hop limit.** Each repeat lowers it by one; at 0 nobody repeats (Meshtastic mesh algorithm). The exception is zero-cost hops: after the first hop, a ROUTER, ROUTER_LATE or CLIENT_BASE keeps the hop limit when the packet's last relay is one of its favourite routers (Meshtastic zero-cost hops, Meshtastic Router.cpp). Default 3, maximum 7 (Meshtastic LoRa).
- **Direct messages, since 2.6.** The first one floods. The sender notes which neighbour relayed the reply and later packets name it as next hop, so only it repeats. Each hop decides for itself; one-way links or old firmware fall back to flooding, and the last retry always floods (Meshtastic mesh algorithm). So a dead relay on a learned route costs retries before messages go around it.
- **Traceroute** shows the route out and back, with the SNR each hop measured on its incoming link, in 0.25 dB steps. Nodes without the channel key, or on old firmware, show as Unknown. Up to 8 hops each way; one every 30 s per sender; it costs more airtime than a text, so use it to diagnose, not to monitor (Meshtastic traceroute).
- **Neighbour lists.** Neighbor Info is off by default. Turned on, it reports a node's direct neighbours with SNR every 6 h (4 h minimum) to the connected app; it goes over LoRa only if "Transmit over LoRa" is on and the primary channel isn't the public default (Meshtastic neighbor info).

**Link margin.** Typical SNR limits to decode: SF7 −7.5 dB, SF8 −10, SF9 −12.5, SF10 −15, SF11 −17.5, SF12 −20 (SX1262 datasheet). Link SNR minus its preset's limit is its margin: a Long Fast link at −12 dB has 5.5 dB; on Medium Fast it would barely work. Check every link before a preset change. Call a link with under 5 dB margin weak (this guide's rule of thumb).

## Finding a failed node

Watch from a node that never moves, such as the hub's. `meshtastic --nodes` lists each node's last-heard time, battery, channel use, transmit airtime, SNR and hops (Meshtastic CLI source). It has no voltage or uptime column unless you add one, for example `meshtastic --nodes --show-fields user.shortName,lastHeard,deviceMetrics.voltage,deviceMetrics.uptimeSeconds`. A relay's own telemetry may come only every 12 h, so ask for it: `meshtastic --request-telemetry --dest '!a1b2c3d4'`, or `--request-telemetry power` for a node with a power sensor fitted, such as an INA219, INA226, INA260 or INA3221 (Meshtastic CLI source, Meshtastic telemetry). The plain request prints battery, voltage, ChUtil, AirUtilTX and uptime. If the hex ID gets no answer, try the node's decimal number (Meshtastic CLI usage).

| Sign | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Not heard for 6 h | Every node sends NodeInfo every 3 h by default (Meshtastic roles): two missed. Traceroute to it |
| Not heard for 24 h, or traceroutes go around it | Dead, flat, or an antenna or coax fault: visit |
| Dawn voltage lower week by week | Snow, shade, a failing panel or a worn battery |
| Battery 101 % (`--nodes` shows it as Powered) | Means charging or no battery: read the voltage (Meshtastic DeviceTelemetry.cpp) |
| Uptime keeps dropping back to near zero | It is restarting: suspect a battery going flat overnight or a loose supply (Meshtastic DeviceTelemetry.cpp) |
| New Unknown hops in traceroutes | A node without your channel key, or on old firmware, is relaying (Meshtastic traceroute) |

**Test schedule.** Weekly: `--nodes` from the hub; log last-heard and voltage. Monthly: traceroute from the hub to each relay, 30 s apart; update the map. Each season and after storms: visits. Twice a year: restore a backup onto a bench node, with the key lines deleted as under Loading a spare, to prove the files and steps work. The node takes the relay's names, role and channel too, so switch it off afterwards.

## Adding a neighbourhood

1. Walk or drive it with a handheld; note where you lose the mesh and the SNR you hear.
2. Check the Site Planner maps saved while the internet worked, then range test from the nearest relay (both in the town guide).
3. Try a CLIENT_BASE on the best roof first, with that neighbourhood's nodes as favourites: it repeats for them without adding a router (Meshtastic role blog). Add a ROUTER only on a high site the area can't reach otherwise, not beside an existing router (Meshtastic role blog).
4. Traceroute from the new area to the hub, draw the links, and give the new node a site card and a backup ([Hand over a town LoRa mesh](#guides/skill_lora_mesh_handover)).

## MeshCore differences

- The repeater CLI has no whole-config export: read settings with `get` and `region`, and `get acl` (serial only), and write them on the site card. A repeater's identity is its private key: `get prv.key` (serial only) shows it, and `set prv.key <hex>` plus a reboot puts it on a spare. Keep that key with the sealed backups, never on the card (MeshCore CLI, MeshCore FAQ).
- Admin is a password, not keys: change the default with `password <new password>` (it is `password` out of the box). Any node that logs in with it joins the admin list, and the reply shows the new password, so do it where nobody can see (MeshCore CLI).
- `neighbors` lists the 8 most recent adverts heard, each with a time and an SNR figure that is four times the dB value; `stats-core` gives battery and uptime, and `stats-radio` noise floor and airtime (both serial only) (MeshCore CLI).
- Repeaters flood an advert every 47 h by default; `dutycycle` (from 1.15; `af` before that) caps a repeater's airtime, 50 % by default, so set it to what your country's rules allow (MeshCore CLI).
